facts.text: Neukölln’s nightlife roots trace back to the 16th‑century Rollkrug tavern near Hermannplatz, a launchpad for the district’s corner‑pub scene.
Neukölln hosts a large number of Sunni mosques, most originally founded for the district’s Turkish Muslim community.
The beer hall Neue Welt, founded as a garden in 1865, became today’s Huxleys Neue Welt concert venue on Hasenheide near Hermannplatz.
The historic Neukölln Water Tower, built in 1928 on the Rollberg hill, now serves as a landmark overlooking the district’s eastern edge.
Neukölln’s three historic cinemas—Neues Off, Passage, and Rollberg Kinos—trace their roots back to a 1919 vaudeville theater, a 1910 movie house, and a 1996 revival.
The Neukölln–Mittenwald railroad, a single‑track line, still operates north of Berlin for industrial transport, linking the district to the city’s outskirts.
